messages:
anya: Quick RFC follow-up — I sketched an alternative lifecycle model for the gateway/edge that I want feedback on. TL;DR: push lifecycle decisions (midstream fallback, retry budgeting, idempotency checks) into the edge, not the client. Pros: simpler client surfaces, centralized observability, single source of truth for soft-fallbacks. Cons: more complexity in the edge and extra state to track.

ben: can you outline the state machine? curious where retry tokens live and how we avoid double-exec on non-idempotent ops.

anya: sure — rough states: ACCEPTED -> HEADERS_SENT -> STREAMING (client->edge->upstream) -> DEGRADED_PENDING (edge decides to fallback midstream) -> FALLBACK_STREAMING -> COMPLETED/ABORTED. Retry budget is per-request, generated at ACCEPTED and passed as an opaque header to upstream: `x-rw-retry-budget: <token>` (signed by edge). Edge only uses budget when the upstream is known-idempotent (based on model config / route metadata).

mike: so the fallback could be a model-variant switch midstream? that worries me for streaming semantics. if we switch to a faster model midstream the client might see content discontinuities. how do we stitch?

anya: good point. idea is to use an intermediate buffering/merge layer in the edge: prefix caching + prefix-merge. when we switch, the edge keeps all tokens emitted so far and continues streaming with tokens from fallback appended. we add metadata frames so client can safely resume without losing order. basically: the client sees a single continuous stream but receives `:source=primary` and `:source=fallback` markers.

rachael: observability/SLIs question — we need to know how often midstream fallback happens per-route and per-customer. can't hide this behind opaque retry tokens.

anya: agreed. edge emits structured events: `fallback_decision` with route, customer_id, reason, time_to_decision, upstream_latency. we also record pre/post-token counts so cost accounting is accurate.

devops-bot: deploy-preview: edge/fallback-proto v0.3 pushed to staging (canary=10%). Logs available: https://staging.logs/rw/edge/fallback-proto/v0.3

ben: security question — that retry-budget token you mentioned, is it replayable? we need it to be single-use or time-limited to avoid abuse.

anya: token contains a short TTL (30s) and a nonce signed with our KMS key. edge invalidates it after use. if a downstream tries replaying after TTL the upstream drops it.

mike: what about partial side effects? for example, a downstream model that triggers billing events midstream. fallback could cause duplicate side-effects if the orig request already executed. How do we handle that?

anya: two mitigations: 1) require route-level metadata `side_effect_policy` (NONE / POSSIBLE / IDEMPOTENT_ONLY). fallback allowed only if NONE or explicitly safe. 2) additive dedupe: all upstreams should accept an `x-rw-request-id` and perform idempotent application for operations flagged as dedupe-capable.

rachael: personally want a feature flag per-tenant to opt into midstream fallback. enterprise customers will likely want it off by default. also add auditing on every decision.

ben: one more nit — clients that maintain long-lived HTTP/2 streams. if we swap upstream, do we rebind the existing TCP connection to a new upstream instance? what's the handoff?

anya: handoff sequence (simplified): edge signals upstream A to quiesce (stop accepting new frames), drain outstanding buffers, then establish connection to upstream B with the same `x-rw-request-id`. edge resumes streaming by replaying necessary KV cache and prefix tokens. We keep the client connection open the whole time — only internal upstream connections are rebinded. There is a short microbuffering window (tens to hundreds ms) to preserve token ordering.

mike: that buffering window needs hard SLO constraints. microbuffers are fine for 99% but the 1% tail could create visible stalls. we need metrics for buffering ms and user-visible latency delta.

anya: noted. metrics: `fallback.buffer_ms`, `fallback.visible_latency_ms`, `fallback.rate_per_min_route`. also a histogram of token gaps.

rachael: we should add an op-level audit log that ties fallback decisions to a human-reviewable trace id. compliance customers will ask for it.

anya: agreed — plan is: 1) metadata header `x-rw-trace-id`; 2) structured fallback event emitted to observability; 3) retention window configurable per-tenant.

ben: ok, sounds workable. next steps?

anya: I'm going to draft a short RFC addendum covering: state machine diagram, header semantics (x-rw-retry-budget, x-rw-request-id, x-rw-trace-id), per-route policy flags (`side_effect_policy`, `allow_midstream_fallback`), metrics list, and a fallback handoff sequence pseudocode block. I'll put it in `docs/rfcs/edge-midstream-fallback.md` and link staging deploy. ping me if you want to pair on the pseudocode test harness.

mike: +1. can we also add a small compatibility test that simulates non-idempotent upstreams to ensure we never fallback incorrectly?

anya: yes — test matrix in RFC draft. thanks all :thumbsup:
